notes: Governing faculty documents: the Provost's Faculty and Family Care Policy web page (approved December 2008; capture 2017-07-01), which the 2016 Faculty Handbook incorporates (3.0, 3.11.3.2, 6.3.2, 6.4.2) and lists as 'UT Family Care Policies for Faculty (PDF)'; the PDF itself is not saved, but the policy text is (web version). missing is false: the Family Care Policy is a governing modified-duties, leave and tenure-clock policy for tenure-stream faculty.

There is no paid parental leave. For nine-month (academic-year) tenure-stream faculty, who accrue neither sick nor annual leave (Handbook 3.3, 6.4.1, 6.4.3), the provisions are: FMDA for the arrival of a child (one semester of teaching release at full pay, research to be negotiated, primary care-giver, twice per career; c1); FMLA 12 workweeks (c5) concurrent with the Tennessee Parental Leave Act's four months (c6), four months total (leave_limits); discretionary unpaid Family Care leave up to one year (c4); discretionary illness leave with or without pay (c8, c9); tenure-clock extension of one year for a birth or adoption (c13).

Handbook 3.0 cites 'Chapter 6.41' for care-giving extensions; no section 6.41 exists in the saved handbook (6.4.1 is sick leave, 6.4.2 family care); read as a reference to 6.4.2 and the Family Care Policy.

Board policy BT0006 (2006) states suspension of the probationary period for any granted leave of absence (c16, general purpose); the 2016 Handbook 3.11.3.2 narrows it to leave under the Family Care Policy (c15). The Family Care Policy attributes to the Board a limit of two one-year extensions, which the saved BT0006 does not state (its two-year extension is 'for good cause related to procedural error'); the limit is coded from the Family Care Policy as use_limit on c13 and c14.

HR0338 lists childbirth and adoption under the four-month TPLA rather than the 12-week FMLA list ('The following events provide an eligible employee up to twelve (12) weeks' names foster care, own and family serious health condition, exigency); the objective and Handbook 6.3.2 include childbirth under FMLA. FMLA coded for birth and adoption as well, concurrent with TPLA. HR0338 calls the state law the 'Tennessee Parental Leave Act'; the baseline row names it TMLA (Tenn. Code 4-21-408). The saved statute is the 2025 edition (amended 2025 ch. 471); its four-month length, 12-month full-time eligibility and three-month notice match HR0338.

TPLA non-birth parent: the statute and HR0338 name 'pregnancy, childbirth and adoption' without role words; HR0338's 'If both spouses e are employees of the university, their combined total of available leave is four (4) months' shows both spouses may use it, so non_birth_parent is coded.

12-month faculty (some administrators and Institute of Agriculture faculty) accrue sick leave (HR0380, c10) and annual leave (c11), which must be used before unpaid FMLA/TPLA leave (HR0338 item 13); recorded under their group name, not counted.

Not components (cannot be used for a birth, or not parental): funeral and bereavement leave (HR0340), court leave, military leave, educational leave (HR0335), faculty development leave (sabbatical for professional projects), administrative leave (HR0355: disaster relief, athletic events, suspension), insurance continuation during leave. Non-discrimination on 'parental status' (Handbook 1.1) is an equal-treatment statement with no leave of its own.

Documents cited but not saved: HR0382 Sick Leave Bank; HR0383 Sick Leave Transfer Between University Employees; HR0373 Personal Leave Day; HR0335 Educational Leave; HR0370 Military Leave; HR0397 Workers' Compensation; HR0220; HR0280; Personnel Policies 305, 315, 335, 370; Manual for Faculty Evaluation; 'UT Family Care Policies for Faculty (PDF)' (web version saved); provost faculty development leave page; Annual Leave Policy.
Calendar: the handbook states semesters ('12 credit hours each semester'; summer semester) without a length, so calendar.kind = semester, and the term length follows R8's order.

Birth parent chain: TPLA 4 months (17.3 weeks) with FMLA 12 workweeks concurrent from the start (four months total, leave_limits) -> FMDA child-arrival semester also available (in addition to family medical leave, no order stated); discretionary: Family Care unpaid leave up to 1 year with FMLA concurrent; nine-month illness leave (no length) with discretionary pay within it; general FMDA reduced load up to 1 year (in lieu of a course-banking arrangement).

Non-birth parent chain: TPLA 4 months with FMLA 12 workweeks concurrent (four months total) -> FMDA child-arrival semester also available if the primary care-giver; discretionary: Family Care unpaid leave up to 1 year with FMLA concurrent.
